title: AI Unlocked: HR & the Future of Work
blurb: For HR professionals and people leaders: recruiting and onboarding acceleration, policy and comms drafting, workforce upskilling design, the HR-AI tool market compared, and the bias/employment-law guardrails that make adoption defensible.

modules.t: People Operations in the AI Era
modules.d: The HR value map — and why HR owns the org’s AI transition.
modules.body:
Landscape

  • Job descriptions, screening support, onboarding content, policy drafting, and survey analysis: immediate acceleration.
  • Bigger: HR designs the workforce transition AI forces on every function — reskilling is now a core HR product.
  • Unchanged: hiring decisions, terminations, and investigations are human judgments with legal weight.
The ILO’s global research finds most jobs will be "transformed rather than destroyed" by generative AI — which makes reskilling, not panic, the professional response. Cathy O’Neil’s warning that algorithms are "opinions embedded in code" completes HR’s mandate: lead the transformation, audit the opinions.

modules.d: JDs, structured interviews, candidate comms, and day-one experiences.
modules.body:
Workflows

  • Inclusive job descriptions drafted and bias-checked; structured interview guides with scoring rubrics (our hiring-packet methodology).
  • Candidate communication sequences — warm, fast, and honest at every stage.
  • Onboarding: role-specific 30/60/90 plans, buddy guides, and searchable policy Q&A (NotebookLM on your handbook).

modules.d: ATS AI vs HRIS assistants vs survey analytics vs general LLMs — and the audit question.
modules.body:
Comparative snapshot

  • ATS AI (Workday/Greenhouse-class features): screening assistance and scheduling — demand the vendor's bias-audit documentation.
  • HRIS assistants (HiBob/BambooHR-class): policy Q&A, analytics narratives inside your system of record.
  • Engagement analytics (CultureAmp-class): theme extraction from surveys at scale.
  • General LLMs: drafting powerhouse for policies, comms, and training — with anonymization discipline.
  • Selection: employment-law exposure per use case × data protection terms × explainability of any scoring.

modules.d: Handbooks, sensitive communication, and investigation support done safely.
modules.body:
Workflows

  • Policy drafting localized to jurisdiction (then legal review); change-communication packs for reorgs and system rollouts.
  • Difficult-conversation preparation: role-played practice before real meetings.
  • Hard line: investigation records and employee personal data never enter consumer AI tools; ER conclusions are human-made.

modules.d: Skills mapping, learning paths, and the org’s AI academy.
modules.body:
Workflows

  • Role-by-role AI-exposure mapping (our MaDSkillz methodology) → reskilling priorities.
  • Learning paths built from curated content + AI-generated practice; champions program design.
  • Measured pilots: hours saved and quality deltas as the business case HR presents to leadership.

modules.d: Policy, pilots, and the upskilling roadmap.
modules.body:
Capstone

  • Your organizational AI-use policy for employees, one recruiting/onboarding workflow live, the tool matrix with legal notes, and a 6-month upskilling roadmap — presented to the panel as if to your executive team.
